newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures surge, nearby months limit-up.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures surge, nearby months limit-up.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended sharply higher on Thursday, with four nearby months up by the daily 400 yen limit on active buying by local investors, traders said.
The benchmark January 1998 contract ended up 310 yen at 15,000 yen per tonne. Daily volume was 124,081 lots.
A stronger Chicago market overnight accelerated buying from individual investors from the opening, and the bullish sentiment remained throughout the session, traders said.
"We see the next target for the December at around 15,400 yen in the near term," a trader said. Backwardation between the spot and the distant month reached 1,790 yen at the close.
The spot March corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.73-1/4 per bushel at 0745 GMT, unchanged from Wednesday's close.
The spot January of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $7.45 at 0745 GMT, up from $7.44-1/2 at Wednesday's close.
